# Getting started

Your documents are the structure of your wiki. This guide is an example page that you can replace in the local workspace.

## Read and navigate

Use the tree on the left to move between pages. Open a folder to see its children, and use **On this page** to jump between the headings of a longer article.

### Direct links

Each page and heading has an address that you can bookmark or share. Relative Markdown links work between folders, too: [visit the coast](../atlas/the-quiet-coast.md).

## Write in Markdown

Open the local workspace and choose **Edit**. The rendered page becomes Markdown, ready to change. **Save** creates a version and publishes it to open browsers.

| Markdown | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `## A heading` | A section in the page index |
| `**important**` | Strong emphasis |
| `[a page](another-page.md)` | A link to another document |

### Organize your pages

Create paths such as `research/observations.md`. Folders are created for you. Renaming or moving a page preserves its history and gives its old address a redirect.

## Revisit an earlier version

Open **History** in the local workspace. Read any saved version or select two revisions to compare their Markdown.

The public site only contains the reading experience. You can stop the local workspace when you finish and keep the public site running.
